tool.name: code_graph_find_definition
tool.description: Find where a symbol is defined in the indexed source tree. Returns file:line for each matching declaration. Use this BEFORE grepping when you need to navigate from a usage to the implementation — one tool call instead of repository-wide search. Symbol matching uses substring containment, so partial names work (e.g. "checkCustomerAccountPermission" matches the full SCIP moniker).

parameter.name: symbol
parameter.description: Symbol name to locate (function, class, type, exported binding). Bare identifier preferred.

returns.description: {"output": "<name> defined at file:line:col"} for each match. {"output": "code graph not available..."} when the indexer was skipped for this target. {"output": "no definition matches found..."} when the symbol isn't in the index.

tool.notes: - The index is pre-built at sandbox setup; queries are read-only and fast. - Returns up to 50 matches. - Falls back to chunk-range location for re-exports / barrel files where SCIP doesn't record a precise enclosing range. - On missing index (eg. unsupported language), output explains the situation — proceed with search_files / read_file instead.
tool.examples:
# Locate the implementation of a middleware
checkCustomerAccountPermission

tool.name: code_graph_find_references
tool.description: Return every place a symbol is referenced in the indexed tree. This is the highest-value query for structural security review: "which routes mount this middleware", "everywhere this auth helper is called", "what depends on this config flag". One call replaces an org-wide grep + manual sift.

parameter.name: symbol
parameter.description: Symbol name to find references for. Bare identifier preferred.

parameter.name: include_definition
parameter.description: Include the definition site in the results. Default false (most callers want references only).

returns.description:
{"output": "<name> — N occurrence(s):
 file:line
 file:line
..."} grouped by matched name (substring matches that resolved to different symbols are listed separately). Capped at 50 results.

tool.notes: - Use for "find all callers of X" questions. Don't grep first if you can ask this. - Locations are chunk-level (line ranges) rather than column-precise — read the file for the specific line if needed. - When the symbol appears in multiple SCIP monikers (eg. similarly-named exports across files), results are grouped by display name so you can see each cluster.
tool.examples:
# Find every place a middleware is mounted on a route
authorizeToParticipantAndAdminRole
# Include the def site too
authorizeToParticipantAndAdminRole true

tool.name: code_graph_find_implementations
tool.description: Return implementations / subtypes of an interface or abstract type. NOT YET SUPPORTED (SCIP relationship blob parsing pending). Tool returns a clear unsupported message; use code_graph_find_references on the interface name as a workaround.

returns.description: {"output": "find_implementations is not yet supported..."} — stub message in W2; W3 will fill this in.

tool.notes: - W2 stub. Calling this won't produce useful results; prefer code_graph_find_references.

tool.name: code_graph_get_imports
tool.description: List the symbols referenced from a given source file. Approximates "what does this file depend on" without reading the whole file. Useful for triaging a router or middleware file before drilling in.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Relative path from the repo root (eg. src/withdrawals/router.ts).

returns.description:
{"output": "<file> references:
 name1
 name2
..."} — distinct symbols mentioned in the file, sorted.

tool.notes: - Superset of declared imports (includes in-file uses of globals). - Capped at 50 distinct symbols.

tool.name: code_graph_get_symbol_at
tool.description: Return symbols mentioned in the chunk containing a given line in a file. Coarser than IDE go-to-symbol (chunk-level, not cursor-precise) but useful for "what does this code reference" lookups.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Relative path from the repo root.

parameter.name: line
parameter.description: Line number (0-indexed, matching how SCIP encodes positions).

returns.description:
{"output": "<file>:<line> mentions:
 name1
 name2
..."} — distinct symbols in the same chunk as that line.

tool.notes: - SCIP chunks are line ranges, not individual lines — expect multiple symbols per call. - Use code_graph_find_references afterwards to drill into a specific symbol's other usages.
